\begin{abstract}
We count the vocabulary of fear in six works of short fiction from Project Gutenberg, three published 1820--1853 and three 1886--1892 (69,870 tokens). A dictionary of fear words finds 22.27 hits per 10,000 tokens in the earlier works and 29.10 in the later ones, but Jekyll and Hyde carries 88 of the 104 later hits, and a hand-checked sample of 20 hits has a precision of 0.75. The key terms of the later works are words of dialogue. The study describes six works, not either period.
\end{abstract}
